title: Bound the package-install sudo keepalive and revoke it on exit
head: b9dce68f32d2
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
outcome: two findings: keepalive keeps refreshing during the Done/Failed prompt until keypress (remaining gap, not regression); EXIT-trap sudo -k can run before an in-flight refresh finishes (stub-reproduced, real-sudo effect from source only). Optional notes in Details.

leads.summary: Both package pickers keep refreshing sudo after the transaction completes while their Done/Failed screen waits for a key
leads.consequence: If a user leaves the picker terminal on the Done/Failed prompt, the sourcing shell stays alive, so the refresh loop continues until its one-hour ceiling even though package work is over. The cached credential can then live for the configured timestamp_timeout after the final refresh. Revoke and stop the loop immediately after pacman/yay/updatedb, before omarchy-show-done blocks for input; the EXIT trap can remain as failure cleanup. This is a source-confirmed execution path, not a runtime reproduction.

leads.summary: The background refresh cannot reach the parent's sudo ticket under ppid timestamps, including tty policy without a terminal
leads.consequence: Initial sudo -v is a child of the sourcing shell; sudo -n true is a child of the background subshell. With timestamp_type=ppid or the documented tty default when no terminal is present, these are distinct tickets. The first noninteractive refresh fails and the loop exits; a long install may prompt again once its initial ticket expires. The new test stub unconditionally succeeds for -n, masking the policy distinction. This is source-confirmed using the Arch sudo 1.9.17p2 ticket implementation, no real sudo was executed.

leads.summary: If exit-time sudo -k fails, the package picker silently reports success while the credential may remain cached
leads.consequence: The final command of the EXIT trap is sudo -k without any status check; Bash preserves the shell's original successful exit. With a stub returning 77 for -k, the caller exits 0 and writes no diagnostic, unlike bin/omarchy-security-functions:71-80, which diagnoses revocation failure and changes success to failure. The real failure condition could leave the active ticket valid until expiration. Check -k and report/fail closed while preserving nonzero original statuses.

leads.summary: Open #13618 edits the same EXIT trap and would drop revocation if its side wins the conflict
leads.consequence: The two PRs diverge, and a merge-file based on the actual original helper leaves an unresolved conflict exactly between this PR's kill/wait/sudo -k trap and #13618's disown/kill-only trap (merged-13618/result:27-33); GitHub also reports CONFLICTING. If manually resolved by retaining #13618's trap, clean exits never call -k; #13618's added update EXIT trap likewise kills the helper but does not itself revoke. Preserve revocation and the current update's independent cleanup when reconciling. No claim is made that these unmerged PRs currently run together.

leads.summary: Reconciling open #13616's new caller without moving its wrapper boundary would prevent its keepalive from renewing any credential
leads.consequence: #13616 adds source omarchy-sudo-keepalive after the channel setup point. On this reviewed head, channel setup has already installed a sudo-no-update PATH wrapper, which converts -v and -n true into sudo -N -v and sudo -N -n true. At sudo 1.9.17p2, -N expressly forbids ticket updates, and sourcing the helper replaces the channel's existing fail-closed EXIT cleanup trap. Both PR heads are divergent and GitHub says CONFLICTING, so this is a conditional integration risk, not current head behavior; manual merge of channel-set and its actual test against the combined version would settle it.

leads.summary: A nonnumeric MAX_REFRESHES override silently turns off renewal while installs still report success
leads.consequence: A value such as OMARCHY_SUDO_KEEPALIVE_MAX_REFRESHES=garbage is a valid environment string but not a count; Bash resolves the undefined arithmetic variable as zero, so the loop runs no refreshes without error. A long package install then prompts again after timestamp_timeout even though the upfront sudo -v succeeded. Require a bounded positive decimal integer or fail visibly before starting the transaction. The analogous interval override is also passed to sleep without validation.

leads.summary: The new test accepts a plausible implementation that revokes at startup but never on clean exit
leads.consequence: The test only asks whether any recorded call equals -k, not whether it is the last sudo call after the install. In a disposable mutant that moves -k directly after -v and removes it from EXIT, all three original tests still pass, including 'clean exit revokes'. Add a final-call/order assertion and a test where the ticket stays active until cleanup. This is a test-fidelity issue below the runtime defects.

limits: Never used host sudo or live sudo timestamps; upstream Arch sudo 1.9.17p2 sources and isolated stubs establish ticket behavior but no native per-PPID end-to-end run was performed.

Full test/cli was attempted in two sandboxed configurations, but both attempts failed at unrelated vscode theme symlink assertion test/cli:607-609; neither is counted as a successful CLI run. The focused CLI metadata check passed separately.
#13616 remains an integration hypothesis because its channel-set file conflicts with the head's rewritten security boundary. No claim of a clean merged run.

flags.claim: omarchy-pkg-install and omarchy-pkg-aur-install make the same calls as at base, plus sudo -k at exit, with the same exit status and output.
A case with no overrides that records the requested sleeps, and one that requires -k after a marker the caller writes last, both fail on those mutants.
A non-numeric OMARCHY_SUDO_KEEPALIVE_MAX_REFRESHES such as abc silently turns refreshing off.
`sudo -k` waits for the key (line 9); `sudo -k` runs only after the keypress (line 104, from my reproducer text).

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** sudo stays refreshed during the Done prompt.

### Refreshes continue during the Done prompt

Both callers end with `omarchy-show-done`, which waits for a key while the shell is alive, so the loop keeps refreshing (up to the 60-refresh cap) and `sudo -k` waits for the key. **Impact:** an unattended Done screen keeps sudo live for up to about an hour (indefinitely at base).

**Suggested change:** put the trap body in a stop function and call it in both callers before `omarchy-show-done`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at b9dce68)</summary>

Test case in the style of the PR's `test/shell.d/sudo-keepalive-test.sh`. It runs the real `bin/omarchy-pkg-install` with stubbed `sudo`, `pacman`, `fzf`, `sleep` and `omarchy-show-done`; the `omarchy-show-done` stub holds the "Press any key" prompt open for 0.5 s. Save it as `test/shell.d/pkg-install-keepalive-test.sh` at the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/pkg-install-keepalive-test.sh`. The real `sudo` is never called.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#
# omarchy-pkg-install needs sudo only for its pacman transaction. Once that is
# done, the keepalive should stop and revoke before the Done/Failed prompt,
# which waits for a keypress for as long as the window stays open.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

mock_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
calls="$test_tmp/calls"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin"

cat >"$mock_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

printf 'sudo %s\n' "$*" >>"$TEST_CALLS"
case ${1:-} in
-v | -k | pacman) exit 0 ;;
-n) [[ ${2:-} == "true" ]] ;;
*) exit 90 ;;
esac
SH

cat >"$mock_bin/pacman" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

printf '%s\n' test-package
SH

cat >"$mock_bin/fzf" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

head -n 1
SH

# Each keepalive interval takes 10 ms here instead of 60 s.
cat >"$mock_bin/sleep" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

exec /bin/sleep 0.01
SH

# Stands in for "Press any key to close...": the window stays open 0.5 s.
cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-show-done" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

printf 'prompt opened (status %s)\n' "$1" >>"$TEST_CALLS"
/bin/sleep 0.5
printf 'prompt closed\n' >>"$TEST_CALLS"
SH

chmod +x "$mock_bin"/*

PATH="$mock_bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" TEST_CALLS="$calls" \
  bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-pkg-install" </dev/null

while_open=$(sed -n '/^prompt opened/,/^prompt closed$/p' "$calls" | grep -c '^sudo -n true$' || true)
(( while_open == 0 )) ||
  fail "no sudo refresh while the Done prompt is open" "refreshes while open: $while_open"$'\n'"$(uniq -c "$calls")"
pass "no sudo refresh while the Done prompt is open"

revoke_line=$(grep -nx 'sudo -k' "$calls" | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f1)
prompt_line=$(grep -n '^prompt opened' "$calls" | cut -d: -f1)
[[ -n $revoke_line ]] && (( revoke_line < prompt_line )) ||
  fail "sudo -k runs before the Done prompt" "$(uniq -c "$calls")"
pass "sudo -k runs before the Done prompt"
```

Actual output at b9dce68 (bash 5.3.15). It failed in 5 of 5 runs, with 38 to 40 refreshes while the prompt was open; this is run 1:

```
refreshes while open: 40
      1 sudo -v
      1 sudo pacman -S --noconfirm test-package
      1 prompt opened (status 0)
     40 sudo -n true
      1 prompt closed
      1 sudo -k
not ok - no sudo refresh while the Done prompt is open
```

At the real 60 s interval, that is one refresh a minute for as long as the prompt stays open, up to the 60-refresh ceiling, which is counted from `sudo -v`. `sudo -k` runs only after the keypress.

Actual output with the keepalive and caller changed as below (5 of 5 runs passed; the PR's `sudo-keepalive-test.sh` also passed 3 of 3 with this keepalive):

```
ok - no sudo refresh while the Done prompt is open
ok - sudo -k runs before the Done prompt
```

The change in `bin/omarchy-sudo-keepalive`, replacing the EXIT trap line:

```bash
# Stop refreshing and revoke. Callers run this once their privileged work is
# done; the EXIT trap runs it otherwise.
omarchy_sudo_keepalive_stop() {
  trap - EXIT
  kill "$SUDO_KEEPALIVE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$SUDO_KEEPALIVE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  sudo -k
}
trap omarchy_sudo_keepalive_stop EXIT
```

The change in `bin/omarchy-pkg-install`:

```bash
  echo "$pkg_names" | tr '\n' ' ' | xargs sudo pacman -S --noconfirm
  status=$?
  omarchy_sudo_keepalive_stop
  omarchy-show-done $status
```

In `bin/omarchy-pkg-aur-install`, `omarchy_sudo_keepalive_stop` goes between `sudo updatedb …` and `omarchy-show-done $code`.
</details>

### `sudo -k` can precede an in-flight refresh

The trap's `kill` ends the loop but not its running `sudo -n true`, so `sudo -k` can run first (stubbed test). **Impact:** per sudo 1.9.17p2's source (untested with real sudo), that refresh can re-enable the record for another `timestamp_timeout`. The window is short.

**Suggested change:** shape the loop like `authorize_update` in `bin/omarchy-update` (`sleep &`, `wait`, TERM trap).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at b9dce68)</summary>

Test case in the style of `test/shell.d/sudo-keepalive-test.sh`. Save it as `test/shell.d/sudo-keepalive-inflight-test.sh` at the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/sudo-keepalive-inflight-test.sh`. `sudo` is a PATH stub, so the real `sudo` is never called.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#
# A refresh that is still running when the caller exits must finish before the
# EXIT trap's sudo -k. Otherwise that refresh can write the timestamp record
# back after it was revoked.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

script="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-sudo-keepalive"
test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

mock_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
calls="$test_tmp/calls"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin"

# The refresh takes 0.3 s, like a slow sudo -n true.
cat >"$mock_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash

case ${1:-} in
-v | -k)
  printf '%s\n' "$1" >>"$TEST_CALLS"
  ;;
-n)
  printf 'refresh-start\n' >>"$TEST_CALLS"
  /bin/sleep 0.3
  printf 'refresh-done\n' >>"$TEST_CALLS"
  ;;
*)
  echo "unexpected sudo command: $*" >&2
  exit 90
  ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$mock_bin/sudo"

# The first refresh starts after one 0.1 s interval; the caller exits at 0.2 s,
# while that refresh is still running.
PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" \
  TEST_CALLS="$calls" \
  OMARCHY_SUDO_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL=0.1 \
  OMARCHY_SUDO_KEEPALIVE_MAX_REFRESHES=5 \
  bash -c '
    source "$1"
    /bin/sleep 0.2
  ' bash "$script"

# Let an orphaned refresh finish before reading the log.
/bin/sleep 0.5

[[ $(tail -n 1 "$calls") == "-k" ]] ||
  fail "sudo -k runs after any in-flight refresh" "$(cat "$calls")"
pass "sudo -k runs after any in-flight refresh"
```

Actual output at b9dce68 (bash 5.3.15; failed in 10 of 10 runs):

```
-v
refresh-start
-k
refresh-done
not ok - sudo -k runs after any in-flight refresh
```

The EXIT trap's `kill` ends the loop subshell at once, but not the `sudo -n true` it started, so `wait` returns and `sudo -k` runs while that refresh is still going.

Actual output with the loop shaped like `authorize_update` in `bin/omarchy-update` (sleep in the background, `wait` for it, and a TERM trap), passed in 10 of 10 runs; the PR's own `sudo-keepalive-test.sh` also passes with this loop:

```
ok - sudo -k runs after any in-flight refresh
```

That loop:

```bash
(
  trap - EXIT
  sleep_pid=""
  trap '[[ -z $sleep_pid ]] || kill "$sleep_pid" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM
  for ((refresh = 0; refresh < keepalive_max_refreshes; refresh++)); do
    sleep "$keepalive_interval" &
    sleep_pid=$!
    wait "$sleep_pid" || exit 0
    sleep_pid=""
    kill -0 "$keepalive_parent_pid" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    sudo -n true 2>/dev/null || exit 0
  done
) &
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (stubbed `sudo`):

- The new test passes at head (90/90, including runs on one contended CPU) and fails against base's keepalive ("expected 3 refreshes, got 16").
- After SIGKILL of the caller, no refresh ran after the kill and the loop had exited; at base it kept refreshing.
- Clean exit, TERM, HUP and SIGINT to the caller's process group run `sudo -k`, stop the loop, and keep the exit status.
- `omarchy-pkg-install` and `omarchy-pkg-aur-install` make the same package and sudo calls as at base (without base's immediate refresh after `sudo -v`), plus `sudo -k` at exit, with the same exit status and output.

**Optional notes:**

- **Optional test improvement:** every case sets both overrides and the `sleep` stub ignores its argument, so changing the default interval to 600 or the ceiling to 100000 still passes. The clean-exit case only checks that `-k` appears somewhere, so a mutant that calls `sudo -k` right after `sudo -v` also passes. A case with no overrides that records the requested sleeps, and one that requires `-k` after a marker the caller writes last, each fails on its mutant.
- A value such as `abc` in `OMARCHY_SUDO_KEEPALIVE_MAX_REFRESHES` silently turns refreshing off (it is evaluated as arithmetic).
- Open PR #13618 also edits `bin/omarchy-sudo-keepalive`; `git merge-tree` reports a conflict there, and resolving it in favour of #13618's EXIT trap would drop the revoke.
</details>
